cases.note: PROMOTED 2026-07-26 (ORPHANED_GAPS 1.6, NCIM r4133 switching cadence). 354-node 138 kV transmission network solved with `set algorithm=NCIM` and model=3 (voltage-regulating) generators whose maxkvar/minkvar Q-limits are ENFORCED (`IgnoreGenQLimits=Yes` is commented out), so it lives or dies on the NCIM PV<->PQ switching cadence. The pinned 0.14.5 oracle predates NCIM entirely (capi_v0145 cannot gate it), and the retired capi015 r4103 cadence -- which the port reproduced loop-for-loop -- ran the PQ->PV test unconditionally every pass, so the generators chattered PV<->PQ around |V| = VTarget and BOTH capi015 and the port stalled at 100 iterations on the (physically correct) fixpoint. Adopting r4133's `if GenModel = 3 ... else ...` mutually-exclusive cadence (Solution.pas l.2059/2166) makes the port converge in EXACTLY r4133's 9 cold iterations at the same node voltages (89_CLINCHRV.1 80072.708834, 1_RIVERSDE.1 76088.991977, 4_NWCARLSL.1 79514.988474; live epri-worker probe 2026-07-26, r4133 warm-resolve 2 iters). LIVE-gated on r4133 with no ledger entry.

CF-C Port 1: CapControl Type=follow ControlSignal=LoadShape. Daily walk over the 24-pt Cap1Shape/Cap2Shape; the two banks switch on the loadshape schedule (cap1 hour 9 ON / hour 24 OFF; cap2 hour 14 ON). check_meters_monitors compares the Cap1Mon/Cap2Mon power channels per step (0 when the bank is open, nonzero when closed), which pins the FOLLOW switching schedule against the oracle. compare_eventlog is intentionally NOT used: the deck runs its own full-day `Solve` at compile (eventlog off), so a post-compile eventlog starts mid-trajectory and the arm/fire step boundary is logged asymmetrically vs the from-scratch oracle run — the switching itself is validated by the monitor power channels and the full per-step voltage compare. Pinned oracle supports FOLLOWCONTROL (not a target-rev feature).

Flipped capi015 -> oracle:r4133 by WP-U2.4 D6 (SwtControl `Action` fix). SwtControl.5_11/7_16/10_14 are created `Action=c` then `edit action=o`; under D6 (r4133) the `action=o` opens the tie switches IMMEDIATELY at parse (the switch state forced like `State`), so the snapshot solve converges in 2 iterations to the open-tie topology. capi015 (Rung-1) instead armed a control-queue action that opened the ties during the solve's control loop (5 iterations, warm-started from the closed mesh), converging to a physically-equivalent-but-not-bit-identical point (node0 V differs 8e-4, above the feeder tier abs floor 1.3e-4 -- a solve-PATH difference, not conditioning). PROVEN the port matches r4133 exactly: r4133 also converges in 2 iters to node0 V=(13261.309423, -34.747502), bit-identical to the port; capi015's 5-iter path gives (13261.308840, -34.748053). All three ties open on every engine (|I|=0). Target-rev case -> no property-compare, so the D12 Normal/State readback (still pinned by the swtcontrol/swt_control unit tests) is moot here. See DIVERGENCES.md §D12 (SwtControl field mapping) + STATUS §WP-U2.4.
